source.notes: A bank of 42 practice items (not an examination paper), 'Competency-based education for CBSE, Item Bank: Science Class 6, September 2021', content created by the British Council for CBSE. Items were written for the NCERT books current in 2021; chapters were mapped by topic to the current NCERT Curiosity (Grade 6) book and must be confirmed. Items have no printed question numbers, so `number` is the printed item identity (e.g. Science6SA1) and `part` the question label inside the item. Answers come from each item's own mark scheme ('Answer' and 'Guidance' columns). Topics not in the current Class 6 book (flowers/pollination, tropism, light and shadows, electromagnets, food spoilage) are left unmapped (chapter null). Many items rely on pictures that are not reproduced.
source.usage: Official CBSE item bank, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in for teachers to use as they wish; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

Thick, woody stem with branches high on the plant.
Thick, woody stem with branching near the base.

questions.text: ‘If we lose the bees, we lose the food.’. Explain why we need to save bees for plants to survive?
extractionIssues: Topic (pollination) is not in the current NCERT Class 6 book; chapter left unmapped

officialAnswer.text: • Bees visit flowers to drink the nectar. (1m) • As they do so the pollen grains stick to their body. (1m) • When they visit another plant the pollen grains get transferred and pollination takes place. (1m) • This process results in the formation of fruits and seeds that give rise to new plants. (1m) • If bee numbers drop, few insects are available to pollinator flowers (1m)

questions.text: Explain any two adaptations observed in a cactus that help it to survive in a desert?

officialAnswer.text: • it has a thick spongy stem that stores water • the leaves are reduced to spines to prevent transpiration • the stem has a waxy coating that prevents loss of water. • Roots grow deep into the soil to tap for ground water. questions.text:
Once upon a time, in a jungle, lived a wolf. One day, he decided to leave his cave and go out and play. On his way, he saw a shadow of a giant figure. He was scared. He was about to run but then realized that it was a shadow of a tree. He started laughing. He moved on and played with his friends. When he was returning back to his cave, the sun had started to set. The setting sun casted shadows of everything everywhere. So, the setting sun casted wolf’s shadow as well. He was extremely happy with his dark figure on the ground. The wolf admired himself. “Why should I run away from the lion? I bet, if I go and growl at him, he will tremble in fear and ask me to be the king.” Suddenly he saw lion not far away from where wolf was standing. He made his way to the lion. When he came near the lion, he growled with all his might. “ I shall rule this jungle.” The lion laughed at the wolf. Then, the lion roared. And before the wolf knew it, he became the lion’s meal. The foolish wolf didn’t know that the sun was playing a trick with him.
Discuss in brief any two characteristics of a shadow that are shown in the story given above.
extractionIssues: Story (source material on page 66) repeated in each part; printed line numbers 5, 10, 15 removed
Topic (shadows) is not in the current NCERT Class 6 book; chapter left unmapped

officialAnswer.text: • Shadows do not tell the exact shape of the object. • Shadows do not tell the exact size of the object. (Guidance: Accept: • Shadows are formed on the other side of the light source. • Shadow of an object is real. (It is formed on the screen) • Shadow of an object is the longest in early morning or late evening. (1 mark each for any two of the given relevant points))

Once upon a time, in a jungle, lived a wolf. One day, he decided to leave his cave and go out and play. On his way, he saw a shadow of a giant figure. He was scared. He was about to run but then realized that it was a shadow of a tree. He started laughing. He moved on and played with his friends. When he was returning back to his cave, the sun had started to set. The setting sun casted shadows of everything everywhere. So, the setting sun casted wolf’s shadow as well. He was extremely happy with his dark figure on the ground. The wolf admired himself. “Why should I run away from the lion? I bet, if I go and growl at him, he will tremble in fear and ask me to be the king.” Suddenly he saw lion not far away from where wolf was standing. He made his way to the lion. When he came near the lion, he growled with all his might. “ I shall rule this jungle.” The lion laughed at the wolf. Then, the lion roared. And before the wolf knew it, he became the lion’s meal. The foolish wolf didn’t know that the sun was playing a trick with him.
Name the property of light that is responsible for the formation of shadow of an object.
extractionIssues: Story (source material on page 66) repeated in each part; printed line numbers 5, 10, 15 removed
Topic (shadows) is not in the current NCERT Class 6 book; chapter left unmapped

officialAnswer.text: Rectilinear propagation of light. (Guidance: Light travels in a straight line or path.)

questions.text:
It was a bright sunny day. Rajat was returning back from his school. He was tired. He sat under a tree covered with a very large number of leaves. There were tiny gaps between the leaves that light could pass through. He saw bright circular patches of light on the ground under the tree. Suddenly, there was a loud noise of an aeroplane in the sky and rushed to see the aeroplane. He was surprised to see that there was no shadow of the aeroplane on the ground. But he had studied that when there is sun and opaque object, shadow is formed on the screen. He was puzzled.
What are the bright patches on the ground? Explain in brief to Rajat about the patches of light under the tree.
extractionIssues: Passage (source material on page 69) repeated in each part; printed line number 5 removed
Topic (pinhole images, shadows) is not in the current NCERT Class 6 book; chapter left unmapped

officialAnswer.text: • These bright circular patches are the pinhole images of the sun. • Small gaps between the leaves act as pinholes. • Sunlight passes through these pinholes to form bright circular images of the sun on the ground. (Guidance: Accept the answer with keywords: • pinhole images of the sun • object – sun • pinhole - tiny gaps between leaves • screen – ground)
